response.query: What explicit decision thresholds will trigger shifting from classical inference to Bayesian partial pooling (e.g., posterior probability, Bayes factor, or minimal detectable effect limits)?
response.answer: Bayesian partial pooling is typically triggered when the posterior probability exceeds 0.95 or when the Bayes factor exceeds 10, indicating strong evidence against the null hypothesis. Minimal detectable effect limits also play a role in deciding when to switch to Bayesian methods.

results.title: Using Bayesian statistics in confirmatory clinical trials in the ...
results.content: This tutorial review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the use of Bayesian statistics in sample size determination, control of type I error rate, multiplicity adjustments, external data borrowing, etc., in the regulatory environment of clinical trials. Generally, complex innovative trial designs have been considered to refer to complex adaptive, Bayesian, and other novel clinical trial designs, but there is no fixed definition because what is considered innovative or novel can change over time [12,13:27–36."),14:2955–72."),15:324–45.")]. For example, Bayesian group sequential designs are increasingly used for seamless modifications in trial design and sample size to expedite the development process of drugs or medical devices, while potentially leveraging external resources [18:333–40."),19:71–80."),20: a multicentre, randomised, sham-controlled trial. Specifically, our focus in this tutorial is on Bayesian sample size determination, which is most useful in confirmatory clinical trials, including late-phase II or III trials in the drug development process or pivotal trials in the medical device development process. Bayesian clinical trial design using historical data that inform the treatment effect.
